In addition, subtle linear low-attenuation cortical channels traversing an otherwise preserved cortex, allowing communication between the intraosseous and soft-tissue components, have been described in approximately 66% of cases (Fig. 4) [6, 45]. Conversely, in a minority of patients (about 17%), the cortex may appear intact on CT, with no visible communication between the intramedullary lesion and the extraosseous soft-tissue component [6, 45], a finding that may contribute to diagnostic uncertainty.

equences with ADC (apparent diffusion coefficient) mapping can be performed. Ewing sarcoma lesions demonstrate low to intermediate T1 signal and variable low to intermediate (68%) or high T2 signal (32%) (Fig. 4) [6, 48, 49]. The areas of high T2 signal on fluid-sensitive sequences may be from hemorrhage, edema, or necrosis; therefore, the length of the tumor should be measured on the T1-weighted sequences since the fluid-sensitive fat-suppressed sequences may overestimate bone marrow involvement, as edema and marrow hyperplasia may show high T2 signal similar to that of tumor [6, 48, 50, 51].
